label: <DEL> step of short sequences, and input w early in the original
explanation: Fires only at the <DEL> step (65% of activation mass) and during the original phase (35%), never in the copy phase. At the delimiter it fires mostly for short sequences (rate falls from about 43% at L=3 to near zero for L>=6). In the original phase it is almost entirely on input w (rate 9x baseline), weaker on g/z/e/t, and peaks at t=3-5. The strongest activations are on a second consecutive w (w w at t=3-4; precision 0.97 for w after w at t 3-5) and on <DEL> right after w. Earlier w/g/e/z/n inputs seem to raise the delimiter activation. The predicate gets 91% of activation mass but precision is only 0.24: many <DEL> steps in short sequences and many early w inputs do not fire, and I could not find a simple condition that separates them. Does not fire at t=0, at t>=8, or on most letters and digits; sequences with digits fire less.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the previous input (most: w, g, e, z, n, t; least: r, 1, d, p) and the current input token, by phase (input phase: w, g, z, e; delimiter step: <DEL>; copy phase: ); timing cues that raise it most: t=3, t=4, L=3 & t=3.
